section_summary.extract_value: This section presents the conclusions of the present study, which investigated sociocultural theory as applied to mindful eating in college women. The findings suggest that limited appreciation of the body's functional qualities helps explain the negative influence of family members' self-objectifying body talk on mindful eating behavior. The authors propose that these results may encourage further development and testing of existing models of adaptive eating styles.
section_summary.evidence_source: 5. Conclusions The present study provided a novel preliminary partial test of sociocultural theory as applied to mindful eating in college women. Results suggest that limited appreciation of the functional qualities of the body helps explain why vicarious exposure to family members' selfobjectifying body talk exerts a negative influence on mindful eating behavior. Findings may stimulate further development and testing of existing contextual and interpersonal models of adaptive eating styles.
